title: Dissector: per-route/model/customer cost and latency breakdown computation
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Problem: The Console needs a single authoritative service that computes fine-grained cost and latency breakdowns by route, model, and customer. Current rollups are coarse (per-tenant hourly totals) and do not explain which component (routing, queuing, model execution, tokenization, post-processing) dominated latency or cost for specific routes or model variants. Billing and SLO teams require both precise chargeback and explainability for regressions.

Goals:
- Produce per-route/model/customer breakdowns that are explainable (component contributions) and accurate to within 2% for hourly rollups and within 5% for near-real-time alerts.
- Support two read patterns: ad-hoc query surface for Console UX (interactive) and nightly export for billing/reconciliation.
- Maintain traceability from any breakdown back to the raw event(s) for auditing.
- Keep additional compute cost bounded: prefer streaming incremental computation with bounded state rather than full reprocessing nightly where possible.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement final billing exports (separate billing pipeline will ingest rollups).
- Does not change existing pricing model inputs; uses current cost-per-GPU-second and per-token cost table via pricing service.
acceptance_criteria: Real-time API endpoint returns per-route/model/customer breakdown with component contributions (model_exec, queue, network, preprocessing, postprocessing) for a 1h window; median API latency < 250ms for cached queries
Hourly rollups written to analytics store (ClickHouse) with per-route/model/customer totals and component shares within 2% of golden batch run
Console UI team can fetch breakdowns via GET /console/v1/breakdowns and render p50/p95 latency and cost columns
All breakdowns link back to raw request IDs for at least 30 days for auditability
Automated tests covering flaky scenarios (fallback routing, model shard spillover) added and green in CI
implementation_notes:
Approach: hybrid real-time + micro-rollup.
1) Ingress: instrumented request events (request_received, routing_decision, model_start, model_end, response_sent) are enriched by the aggregator service with model profile data (per-model latency-per-token, quantized kernel selection), pricing lookup (current cost rates), and route-level config.
2) Per-request decomposition: compute component durations and attribute cost fractions using a simple fractional apportionment algorithm: baseline attribution to observed durations, then normalize by model-specific compute efficiency for model_exec. This yields a vector of (latency_ms, cost_usd) per component.
3) Streaming materialization: a Flink job (or internal stream-processor) consumes enriched events and maintains bounded keyed state per (route, model, customer) using time-windowed micro-rollups (1m micro-slices aggregated into hourly rollups). Micro-rollups kept small (statistical sketches for heavy hitters, exact counters for top N routes).
4) Store: near-real-time read surface stored in a low-latency materialized view (ClickHouse for Console reads) plus archival hourly rollups in BigQuery for billing and reconciliations.
5) Backfill: deterministic batch job can recompute hourly rollups for reconciliation using raw events if drift > 2%.

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Why hybrid? Pure batch yields perfect accuracy but high latency for SLO alerts; pure per-request storage is too expensive. Micro-rollups balance compute and fidelity.
- Attribution method: we intentionally avoid complex ML attribution models for now; deterministic fractional attribution is easier to audit and debug. Revisit if systematic bias appears.
- Storage: ClickHouse chosen for fast Console queries; BigQuery chosen for long-term reconciliation and billing exports. Both stores receive the same canonical hourly rollup schema for consistency.
api_surface: GET /console/v1/breakdowns/{breakdown_id}?trace=true -> returns breakdown with list of representative request_ids for audit
POST /internal/v1/rollups/recompute -> trigger deterministic recompute for a given window (auth: backend-only)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): deploy streaming processor in canary cluster keyed to 5% of routes (low traffic) and mirror outputs to a shadow ClickHouse table. Validate against golden batch. Phase 2 (90-day ramp): increase to 25% then 75% with performance monitoring on CPU/GPU of stream job. Phase 3: switch console reads to materialized view and enable hourly export to billing dataset. Emergency rollback: toggle route-level mirror flag; run batch recompute to restore authoritative rollups.
testing_plan: Unit tests for apportionment logic and edge cases (zero-duration components, overlapping model_start/model_end, missing events). Integration test harness using recorded production event streams (anonymized) to validate drift < 2% vs batch. Load test of streaming job at 2x peak QPS. E2E smoke for Console read path and billing export ingestion.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Arielle Park: Kickoff meeting notes attached to design doc. Agreed hybrid approach; prioritized reproducibility over speculative ML-based attribution.

2026-03-04 - Mateo Singh: Implemented initial apportionment function and local unit tests. Observed edge-case where model_end missing for timed-out requests; treating as model_end = last_seen + estimated_kv_flush_time for now.
2026-03-06 - Priya Malhotra (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria — asked to ensure linkability to raw request ids for auditing. Mateo: added trace field and storage plan.
2026-03-09 - Security review (prelim): flagged pricing lookup service auth; added backend-only POST for recompute and RBAC to streaming consumer. Security ticket created: ENG-48200.

2026-03-11 - QA: Found non-determinism in micro-rollup merging across partitions during failover. Root cause: clock skew in consumer hosts; mitigation: switch to event-time watermarks and deterministic merge key. Added to implementation tasks.
2026-03-12 - Mateo Singh: Deployed canary for three low-traffic routes in staging. Shadow outputs match batch within 1.1% on test data. Starting Grafana dashboard for drift and lag monitoring.
notes: Fallback behavior: if pricing lookup fails, attribute cost using last-known snapshot for that customer and emit a warning metric.
Retention: micro-rollups kept for 7 days in ClickHouse and hourly rollups for 3 years in BigQuery for billing and audits.
Open question: whether to expose component-level cost to customers in billing UI; flagged for PM discussion (PM ticket PM-412).
